title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 1 Lesson 1: Resolving Force Components custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A force of magnitude $50\text{ N}$ acts at an angle of $35^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis. Calculate the component of the force in the positive $x$-direction, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

A force of magnitude $40\text{ N}$ acts at an angle of $25^\circ$ to the upward vertical ($y$-axis). Calculate the horizontal component of the force, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

A force of magnitude $65\text{ N}$ acts at an angle of $40^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis, pointing into the second quadrant. State the $x$-component of this force, taking the positive direction as to the right.
A block of mass $6\text{ kg}$ rests on a plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the component of the weight of the block acting down the slope.
A force of magnitude $75\text{ N}$ acts at an acute angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\theta = \frac{3}{4}$. Find the exact vertical component of the force.

A particle on an inclined plane is acted on by a pulling force of magnitude $80\text{ N}$ directed at an angle of $20^\circ$ above the line of greatest slope. Calculate the component of this pulling force perpendicular to the plane, directed away from the surface, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: Two forces of magnitudes $20\text{ N}$ and $30\text{ N}$ act at a point $O$ on a horizontal plane. The $20\text{ N}$ force acts along the positive $x$-axis. The $30\text{ N}$ force acts at an angle of $60^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total component of the two forces in the positive $x$-direction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total component of the two forces in the positive $y$-direction, giving your answer in exact surd form and correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A box of mass $8\text{ kg}$ lies on a smooth horizontal floor. A rope attached to the box pulls it with a tension of $50\text{ N}$ at an angle of $28^\circ$ above the horizontal. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the horizontal component of the tension force pulling the box forward, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the upward vertical component of the tension force, and hence find the normal contact force $R$ exerted by the floor on the box.

questions.prompt:
Three coplanar forces of magnitudes $15\text{ N}$, $25\text{ N}$, and $20\text{ N}$ act at a point $O$.
- The $15\text{ N}$ force acts along the positive $x$-axis.
- The $25\text{ N}$ force acts at an angle of $40^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis.
- The $20\text{ N}$ force acts at an angle of $70^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis in the third quadrant.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the total resolved component of the three forces in the $x$-direction, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the total resolved component of the three forces in the $y$-direction, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $5\text{ kg}$ is placed on a plane inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{7}{24}$. A horizontal pushing force of magnitude $30\text{ N}$ acts on the block directed into the plane. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State the exact values of $\sin\alpha$ and $\cos\alpha$, and calculate the component of the weight of the block acting down the plane.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total component of the applied $30\text{ N}$ horizontal force and the weight acting perpendicular to the inclined plane.

questions.prompt: A force of magnitude $P\text{ N}$ acts at an acute angle $\theta$ to the positive $x$-axis. Together with a fixed force of $24\text{ N}$ acting along the negative $x$-axis and a fixed force of $10\text{ N}$ acting along the positive $y$-axis, the net resolved component in the $x$-direction is $12\text{ N}$ and the net resolved component in the $y$-direction is $28\text{ N}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the values of $P\cos\theta$ and $P\sin\theta$, and hence show that $\tan\theta = 0.5$. Find the value of $\theta$ in degrees correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the exact value of $P$ in simplified surd form, and also give its value correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt:
Three coplanar forces act at the origin $O$:
- A force $F_1 = 20\text{ N}$ along the positive $x$-axis.
- A force $F_2 = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$ at an angle of $45^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis.
- A force $F_3 = 20\text{ N}$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis in the second quadrant.
A reference axis $u$ passes through $O$ and is inclined at $30^\circ$ anticlockwise to the positive $x$-axis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the exact component of each of the three forces along the positive $x$-axis, and hence find the exact net component $X$ in the $x$-direction in terms of $\sqrt{3}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By resolving directly along the line of the $u$-axis (at $30^\circ$ to the positive $x$-axis), find the exact total resolved component of the three forces along the $u$-axis.

questions.prompt: A sledge of mass $m = 12\text{ kg}$ is held on a smooth slope inclined at an angle of $25^\circ$ to the horizontal. A pulling force of magnitude $T\text{ N}$ is applied to the sledge at an angle of $15^\circ$ above the line of greatest slope. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Express the component of the weight of the sledge parallel to the slope down the incline, and the component of the pulling force $T$ parallel to the slope up the incline. Hence find the value of $T$ required for the net force parallel to the slope to be zero, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the value of $T = 52.5\text{ N}$ from part (a), calculate the normal contact force $R$ exerted by the slope on the sledge, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: The angle of the pulling force to the slope is kept at $15^\circ$, but the magnitude of $T$ is increased. Find the critical value of $T$ at which the sledge is on the point of lifting off the slope, and state the resulting acceleration of the sledge up the slope at this instant.
